operational-example.copy: Use Chip for compact filters, attributes, or suggested values that need selection, removal, or quick recognition without becoming a full Button.

scenario.title: Active dashboard filters
rationale: Chips keep applied criteria visible near the content they affect.
Selected and removable states are explicit instead of hidden in a filter summary.
Chip is compact enough for filter bars, tables, and cards.

items.rule: Owns pill shape, border, surface, density, and focus.
Names the filter, attribute, or suggestion in plain language.
Optional icon supports recognition without replacing the label.
Optional close icon removes an applied criterion and keeps a named action.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, focus, pressed, selected, hover, default
items: Use button semantics when Chip is interactive.
Expose selected state with aria-pressed when it toggles.
Give removable chips a clear remove action.
Keep the visible label as the accessible name.
Do not rely on color alone for selected state.

variants.copy: Chip variants describe whether the pill filters, displays an input token, suggests a value, or works as a compact assistive action.

states.copy: Chip states communicate availability, hover, press, focus, selection, and disabled context while the pill size remains stable.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines chip purpose; state defines interaction. Disabled wins before focus, press, selected, hover, and default.

full-width.copy: Chip keeps intrinsic width. Containers may wrap or scroll chip groups, but an individual chip does not stretch.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Responsive chip groups wrap in roomy layouts and scroll horizontally only when filters must stay on one line.

viewport-organization.copy: Use chips as scan-friendly filters in mobile stacks and dense dashboards, but move complex filtering into patterns.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Show the highest-value filters first and allow wrap.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Use grouped filter rows with clear removal.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use chip sets near tables or dashboards without replacing filter forms.

playground.copy: Use the playground to test label length, selected state, removable affordance, icon, and variant before placing Chip in filter bars or data surfaces.

api-foundations.copy: Chip API exposes label, variant, state, selected, removable, and optional icon while Design System foundations own surface, focus, density, and motion.

props.name: interactive
props.notes: Forces button semantics when Chip previews an interactive state.

props.name: state
props.notes: Interaction state: default, hover, pressed, selected, focus, or disabled.

props.name: tone
props.notes: Optional semantic treatment for warning or danger filters.

props.name: variant
props.notes: Purpose variant: filter, input, suggestion, or assist.

props.name: removable
props.notes: Shows remove affordance and enables remove behavior.

props.name: onRemove
props.notes: Called when a removable chip is removed.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for compact filters, input tokens, and suggestions.
Use removable only when the chip can be cleared.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use Chip for primary actions.
Do not hide complex filters in chip-only UI.
Do not use selected state as decoration.

groups.title: Review
items: Confirm remove behavior and focus order.

rejectIf: Chip replaces a Button for primary action.
Remove icon has no accessible action.
Chip group hides required filter controls.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Chip as a compact filter or token decision: agents can assemble labels and selected/removable states when the filter meaning is explicit, while humans own policy and grouping.
canDecide: Use Chip for active filters, input tokens, suggestions, or compact attributes.
Set selected and removable when product behavior is explicit.
Choose icons only when they clarify the visible label.
mustAsk: The chip changes permissions, cost, compliance, or hidden filter logic.
The filter grouping or source of truth is unclear.
The chip might be a Button, Tab, or Select instead.
rejectIf: Chip is used as the primary action.
Remove behavior is unclear or destructive.
miel.handoff: I am using Chip for compact filter or token UI. I need confirmation on filter source, selected/removable behavior, and whether a larger pattern owns the group.
